FEASIBILITY NUDGE:

ROUTABLE SUBSTRATE: cavity_2d_cfd
SUBSTRATE CONTRACT: cavity_2d

1. WHAT THE INSTRUMENT IS
This substrate runs 2D incompressible laminar cavity-class cases: a closed
box of fluid driven by one or more moving walls (the classic lid-driven
cavity and its variants). The solver is OpenFOAM v12 running inside a
container, driven through the run_cfd wrapper — deterministic Python with no
AI inside, which launches the case's declared solver application and reads
the resulting log. The validated envelope comes from the spike: a 1 m square
cavity, 64x64 mesh, lid at 2 m/s, kinematic viscosity 0.01 m^2/s (Reynolds
number 200), laminar, converged. Cases near that class are proven; anything
far outside it is unproven, not impossible.

2. WHAT A CASE MUST DEFINE
A case is a complete, self-contained directory the solver can run as-is.
It must define:
  - geometry and mesh: the cavity shape and its cell resolution (a blockMesh
    description is built automatically if a mesh dictionary is present and
    no mesh exists yet);
  - boundary velocities: which walls move and how fast, and which are
    stationary no-slip walls;
  - the fluid's kinematic viscosity;
  - steady vs. transient treatment and an end time: the case's own control
    dictionary declares the solver application, the end time, and the time
    step — the wrapper reads these, it does not choose them.

3. WHAT run_cfd RETURNS TODAY
On a run that completes, a small fixed summary — never the full solver log:
  - converged: true or false. The EXACT definition: the run's final
    simulated time reached the case's declared end time (within one time
    step), AND every field residual recorded at the start of the final time
    step is below 1e-3. Both must hold; "finished cleanly" alone is not
    converged.
  - residuals: the per-field residuals from the final time step, as parsed
    from the solver log.
  - final time: the last simulated time the solver reached.
  - Courant number: the maximum reported Courant number.
  - continuity error: the last reported global continuity error.
  - runtime: solver execution time and wall-clock seconds.
  - qoi (OPTIONAL, on request): the wrapper can extract ONE quantity of
    interest per run from fields the case already wrote, at the latest
    written time, using the solver's own stock post-processing machinery.
    Supported operations: volAverage | min | max | volIntegrate over one
    existing field, with an optional component (e.g. mag for a vector's
    magnitude, or 0|1|2 for a single component). On success the summary
    gains qoi {name, field, operation, value, time}. QoI extraction
    requires the run to have reached its declared end time; convergence is
    reported separately, and a QoI from an unconverged run is reported
    without endorsement — judging whether such a value is usable is
    downstream judgment, not the wrapper's.
  - qoi_error: on ANY extraction failure (missing field, post-processing
    error, unparseable output) the summary carries qoi_error with an
    honest reason and NO qoi block — the instrument never fabricates a
    number.
  - qois (OPTIONAL, on request): instead of a single QoI, a VECTOR of
    quantities of interest may be extracted from ONE solved case in a single
    pass. Each entry names a reduction — min | max | volAverage — over an
    existing field (U or p; a vector component is chosen with mag for the
    magnitude or 0|1|2 for one component). Each reduction may additionally
    carry a deterministic spatial mask that restricts it to part of the
    domain: corner_exclusion {radius_frac} drops cells within that fraction
    of the domain size of any corner; boundary_exclusion {distance_frac}
    keeps only cells at least that fraction of the domain size away from any
    wall; box {x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max as domain fractions} keeps only the
    cells inside that fractional box. A masked result reports the number of
    cells masked and the total cell count beside its value. Each entry
    succeeds or fails independently, exactly as the single-QoI path does — a
    bad entry yields a per-entry qoi_error and NO number, never a fabricated
    value. Alongside the vector, a COMPACT FIELD EXPORT is written for
    offline analysis: cell centres and cell volumes plus the final U and p
    fields, saved as an on-disk array file, with only a small summary (its
    path, the field list, the cell count, and per-field min/max/mean)
    returned — the raw field arrays never cross back into any stage.
On a failed run: converged is false and only a bounded set of error lines
(at most 40) explaining the failure is returned. A run is killed after 600
seconds of wall-clock time and reported as a failure.
Indicative cost, measured on this substrate (64x64 mesh, transient): the
per-step solver rate is a RANGE of 2.3-4.1 ms/step, not a single fixed rate,
and wall-clock time scales with Reynolds number — measured points are ~9.2-9.3 s
for baseline short runs and 161-175 s for Re 100-1600 sweep runs (the latter
versus the ~95 s a stale single-rate estimate once predicted). Wall-clock
includes container exec, meshing, and log-parsing overhead.

4. HONEST LIMITS
  - 2D laminar flow only. There are no turbulence models; a case whose
    physics is actually turbulent will not be simulated correctly and the
    wrapper cannot detect that.
  - Field-derived QoIs come ONLY from fields the solved case actually
    wrote. For this substrate that means velocity- and pressure-field
    statistics (e.g. volume-averaged |U|, min/max/integral of p) YES;
    concentration fields NO: the incompressible laminar solve carries no
    scalar-transport / tracer physics, so no concentration field exists to
    read, and concentration-derived mixing QoIs remain unextractable. No
    new fields the case didn't write. A spec may still request an
    unservable QoI — judging whether the instrument can feasibly serve a
    spec is the fidelity gate's job, not stage 2's.
  - Post-processing reads the latest written time only: a single QoI or a
    whole VECTOR of QoIs (each optionally spatially masked) plus the compact
    field export are all taken from that one final written state. There is no
    time-series extraction, no probes, and no field sampling other than the
    volume reductions (masked or whole-domain) and the field export listed
    above — nothing before the final time can be read.
  - A masked extremum is only as trustworthy as its mask is honest, and two
    rules follow. (i) A masked extremum MUST state its mask type and its
    parameters in the spec — an extremum whose masking region is left
    unstated is not interpretable. (ii) A masked-extremum TREND should be
    demonstrated mask-insensitive — the value stays stable as the exclusion
    region grows — before it is relied on, because a mask that merely clips a
    boundary singularity by a little still reports that singularity. Measured
    example on this substrate: the interior minimum of p at Re 100 is -0.270
    with a corner-exclusion radius of 0.05 but only -0.141 at radius 0.10 — a
    roughly two-fold swing, so this particular extremum is NOT yet
    mask-insensitive and its trend must not be trusted without a
    wider-radius check.
  - Convergence is judged from residuals and end time only; it says the
    solver settled, not that the physics is resolved (mesh-independence is
    nobody's promise here).
  - Whether a case's regime assumptions are themselves trustworthy is NOT
    checked anywhere in this contract; that open axis belongs to the
    fidelity gate's future work, and nothing here should be read as
    covering it.

5. CANONICAL PARAMETER VOCABULARY
The case builder honors exactly these canonical parameter names; a run
whose parameters use them (with plain numeric values) can be synthesized
into a runnable case:
  - kinematic_viscosity  (m^2/s) — the fluid's kinematic viscosity
  - lid_velocity         (m/s)   — the moving-wall speed
  - cavity_length        (m)     — the cavity's side length (uniform scaling)
  - mesh_resolution      (cells per side) — N, meshed as N x N x 1
  - end_time             (s)     — simulated end time
  - time_step            (s)     — solver time step
Reynolds number is never buildable directly: specify lid_velocity,
cavity_length, and kinematic_viscosity, and Re may be stated as a derived
quantity (it will be verified against that decomposition, not honored on
its own). Parameters beyond this vocabulary remain fully legitimate when
the hypothesis genuinely requires them — but the current builder cannot
honor them and will halt loudly, by name, on any it does not know.


ROUTABLE SUBSTRATE: calculix_cantilever_fea
SUBSTRATE CONTRACT: calculix_cantilever_fea

1. WHAT THE INSTRUMENT IS
This substrate runs 3D linear-elastic isotropic small-deflection static
cantilever beams: a rectangular prism clamped on one end face, loaded by a
single transverse force distributed over the opposite end face. The solver
is CalculiX 2.17 (ccx) running inside the ccx-prod container, driven
through the run_fea wrapper — deterministic Python with no AI inside,
which meshes the beam, writes the input deck, runs one static solve, and
parses the result down to a small summary. The element is C3D8I, the
8-node incompatible-modes hexahedron: bending-capable IN THE ELEMENT
FORMULATION itself, so this family has no element-order knob to set and a
coarse mesh does not shear-lock (contrast the sibling fenicsx cantilever
family, which exposes element order as typed input). The validated
envelope comes from this substrate's own evidence: the reference beam
(L=1.0 m, w=h=0.05 m, steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, 1000 N) at three
refinements reproduces the Euler-Bernoulli closed form within 1.466% ->
0.602% -> 0.550% (mesh 8 -> 16 -> 32), converging monotonically from
below, and the calibration battery executed 2026-07-16 scored 30/30 gate
draws in-band at 3 repeats with the wrapper's five typed-rejection
self-checks 5/5. Cases in that class are proven; anything far outside it
is unproven, not impossible.

2. WHAT A CASE MUST DEFINE
A case is a fully typed input; the wrapper meshes and solves it as-is. It
must define, in the canonical vocabulary of section 5: the beam's three
dimensions; the isotropic material's Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio;
the total transverse tip load; and the mesh density along the length.
Geometry convention: X spans the length (clamped at x=0), Y the width, Z
the height and the load direction (-Z). Every field is REQUIRED — there
are no defaults, an omitted field is a named rejection, never a guess —
and unknown fields are rejected by name. Nothing else is meshable by this
instrument: any other geometry, boundary condition, material law, or load
pattern is outside it.

3. WHAT run_fea RETURNS TODAY
On a run that completes, a small fixed summary — never the raw solver
output:
  - valid: true or false. False whenever the input was rejected, the
    solver failed, or the output was unusable; diagnostics names the
    reason, and the instrument NEVER fabricates a number.
  - qoi (on a valid run), carrying BOTH of these, every run, with no
    per-run selection:
      * tip_displacement (m): the maximum |u3| over the printed nodes —
        the tip deflection of a transversely loaded cantilever. VALIDATED
        within family v1 against the Euler-Bernoulli closed form.
      * max_von_mises (Pa): the maximum von Mises stress over the
        integration points. REPORTED-ONLY — see the regime statement
        below and section 4.
  - diagnostics: a bounded human-readable line (mesh and node/element
    counts, parse summary), capped at 800 characters.
  - runtime_s: wall-clock seconds. A run is killed after 600 seconds and
    reported as a failure; one retry on transient infrastructure failure.
An experiment spec's qoi object may carry the machine-readable key
"quantity" naming which returned number is THE quantity of interest —
exactly one of "tip_displacement" | "max_von_mises", validated against
the wrapper's own vocabulary; a qoi without it is recorded honestly as
not extractable, never guessed.
How this summary maps to an upstream stage-4 run entry (per the ngspice
mapping, stated here at enrollment): converged := (valid is true) — for
this substrate converged means the solve COMPLETED AND PARSED, never that
the mesh is converged or the physics in-regime; wall_clock_s :=
runtime_s; valid=false carries the wrapper's own diagnostics line as
qoi_error, and no number is ever invented. There is no `state` key: this
wrapper's summary carries no state vocabulary of its own, only the
boolean valid.
THIS INSTRUMENT'S REGIME (stated at enrollment per R-23.5-5c; shape
ruled Packet B Phase 2.0, build chat under the owner's standing
delegation, 2026-07-17): not a Reynolds band, not a circuit analysis,
and not a symbolic operation — this instrument serves exactly one
physics regime by construction: linear-elastic isotropic
small-deflection STATIC bending of a singly-clamped, tip-loaded
rectangular prism, solved with the C3D8I incompatible-modes hex element
(bending-capable in the element formulation itself, so this family has
no element-order knob to set). The regime's ruled bounds are card
judgments the gate reads, not typed inputs: the Euler-Bernoulli
reference applies at slenderness length/height >= 10 (F1); the linear
solve holds to tip-deflection/length <= 0.10 (F2); a mesh must reproduce
the reference within 2.0% (F3); and max_von_mises is REPORTED-ONLY,
never validated (F4) — its pointwise maximum sits on the clamped-corner
stress singularity and RISES with mesh refinement (measured 2.521e7 ->
3.848e7 Pa across mesh 8 -> 32) instead of settling, so a claim resting
on it is deferred, never trusted. An experiment spec's required "regime"
object for this substrate is {"notes": "..."} — a statement of why the
case sits inside those bounds; a regime block carrying Reynolds fields,
an analysis_type key, or an operation key is rejected by name by the
per-substrate validator before anything runs. Documentation honesty: the
docs index serves the CalculiX manual v2.23 while the solver is v2.17 —
a superset reference, not a version-matched one; a worked example from
the manual must be version-checked before its numbers are trusted.

4. HONEST LIMITS
  - Linear-elastic isotropic small-deflection statics ONLY. No
    plasticity, no hyperelasticity, no contact, no buckling, no dynamics,
    no anisotropy, no thermal coupling, no distributed or multiple loads,
    no non-rectangular sections. A case whose physics is actually any of
    those will still return a number, and the wrapper cannot detect that.
  - The Euler-Bernoulli closed form delta = P*L^3/(3*E*I) with
    I = w*h^3/12 is the only reference this instrument is validated
    against, and it is only itself trustworthy for SLENDER beams — it
    neglects shear deformation, whose correction grows rapidly below
    length/height = 10 (bound F1). A stubby beam needs a Timoshenko or
    full-elasticity reference; the solve may be fine, but
    validated-against-the-reference no longer holds.
  - Past tip-deflection/length ~ 0.10 (bound F2) the small-deflection
    assumption itself is broken: the linear static solve ignores
    geometric stiffening and over-predicts deflection while converging
    cleanly. No re-run of THIS instrument fixes that.
  - max_von_mises is REPORTED, NOT VALIDATED (bound F4): its pointwise
    maximum sits at the clamped-corner stress singularity, which belongs
    to the continuum problem itself — it rises with refinement (measured
    2.521e7 -> 2.609e7 -> 3.848e7 Pa across mesh 8 -> 16 -> 32) instead
    of settling and has no converged value to find. The sibling fenicsx
    instrument measured the same rise independently on a different
    solver: the disease is the corner, not the code.
  - A case with nu near 0.5 is numerically suspect even though the input
    is well-formed and the solve converges: near-incompressibility risks
    volumetric locking, which this element is not built to remedy.
    Anticipated from the physics, not measured on this substrate.
  - There is NO regime check anywhere in this instrument. It confirms
    that the solver ran and the output parsed — never that the physics
    is in-regime, never that the mesh is converged. Slenderness and
    linearity are invisible to it.
  - Whether a case's regime assumptions are themselves trustworthy is
    NOT checked anywhere in this contract; that open axis belongs to the
    fidelity gate's future work, and nothing here should be read as
    covering it.

5. CANONICAL PARAMETER VOCABULARY
The wrapper honors exactly these canonical parameter names; anything
else is rejected by name, and every one is REQUIRED (no defaults — an
omitted field is a rejection, never a guess):
  - length        (m)   -- beam length, spanning X; clamped at x=0
  - width         (m)   -- section width, spanning Y
  - height        (m)   -- section height, spanning Z; the load direction
  - E             (Pa)  -- Young's modulus; must be positive
  - nu            (-)   -- Poisson's ratio; must be in (-1, 0.5)
  - tip_load      (N)   -- total transverse load at x=length, in -Z,
                           distributed uniformly over the tip face
  - mesh_density  (int) -- hexahedral element count along the length; the
                           width and height counts scale by aspect ratio,
                           so the reference beam meshes 8 -> 8x1x1,
                           16 -> 16x1x1, 32 -> 32x2x2
These seven names carry the SAME units and semantics as the sibling
fenicsx cantilever family v1, deliberately, so one beam can be posed to
both instruments; that family's eighth field (element_degree) has no
counterpart here — C3D8I fixes bending locking in the element
formulation instead, with no order to choose.


ROUTABLE SUBSTRATE: fenicsx_cantilever_elastic
SUBSTRATE CONTRACT: fenicsx_cantilever_elastic

1. WHAT THE INSTRUMENT IS
This substrate runs 3D linear-elastic isotropic small-deflection static
cantilever beams: a rectangular prism clamped on one end face, loaded by a single
transverse force distributed over the opposite end face. The solver is FEniCSx /
DOLFINx 0.11.0.post0 (real-mode PETSc, float64) running inside the dolfinx-prod
container, driven through the run_fenicsx wrapper -- deterministic Python with no
AI inside, which meshes the beam, solves one linear system, and reads the result.
This is FEniCSx (import dolfinx), NOT legacy FEniCS (from dolfin import), which
last released in 2019 and does not run here.

The element is Lagrange (continuous, vector-valued) of a degree the CASE chooses:
element_degree is typed input, not a fixed property of the instrument. That choice
is a physics decision, not a preference -- see the honest limits.

2. WHAT A CASE MUST DEFINE
A case is a fully typed input; the wrapper meshes and solves it as-is. It must
define, in the canonical vocabulary below: the beam's three dimensions; the
isotropic material's Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio; the total transverse
tip load; the mesh density along the length; and the element degree. Geometry
convention: X spans the length (clamped at x=0), Y the width, Z the height and
the load direction (-Z). Nothing else is meshable by this instrument: any other
geometry, boundary condition, material law, or load pattern is outside it.

3. WHAT run_fenicsx RETURNS TODAY
On a run that completes, a small fixed summary -- never the raw solver output:
  - valid: true or false. False whenever the input was rejected, the substrate
    was unreachable, the solve failed, or the output was unusable.
  - qoi (on a valid run), carrying BOTH of:
      * tip_displacement (m): the maximum |u_z| over the displacement field's
        degrees of freedom. For Lagrange elements these are point evaluations at
        the element's dof coordinates -- mesh nodes at degree 1, and nodes plus
        edge/face/interior points at degree 2 and above.
      * max_von_mises (Pa): the pointwise maximum von Mises stress, computed by
        interpolating the stress derived from the displacement into a
        discontinuous space of degree (element_degree - 1) and taking the maximum
        over that space's dofs.
  - diagnostics: a bounded human-readable string (solver version, element family
    and degree, mesh size, cell and dof counts, scalar type, solve time), capped
    at 800 characters.
  - runtime_s: wall-clock seconds.
On any failure: valid=false, qoi=null, and diagnostics names the reason. The
instrument NEVER fabricates a number. A run is killed after 600 seconds of
wall-clock time and reported as a failure.
An experiment spec's qoi object may carry the machine-readable key
"quantity" naming which returned number is THE quantity of interest —
exactly one of "tip_displacement" | "max_von_mises", validated against
the wrapper's own vocabulary; a qoi without it is recorded honestly as
not extractable, never guessed.
How this summary maps to an upstream stage-4 run entry (per the ngspice
mapping, stated here at enrollment): converged := (valid is true) —
COMPLETED AND PARSED, never mesh-converged, never in-regime, never
element-appropriate; wall_clock_s := runtime_s; valid=false carries the
wrapper's own diagnostics line as qoi_error, and no number is ever
invented. There is no `state` key: this wrapper's summary carries no
state vocabulary of its own, only the boolean valid.
THIS INSTRUMENT'S REGIME (stated at enrollment per R-23.5-5c; shape
ruled Packet B Phase 2.0, build chat under the owner's standing
delegation, 2026-07-17): not a Reynolds band, not a circuit analysis,
and not a symbolic operation — this instrument serves exactly one
physics regime by construction: linear-elastic isotropic
small-deflection STATIC bending of a singly-clamped, tip-loaded
rectangular prism. Its ruled bounds are card judgments the gate reads:
slenderness length/height >= 10 (G1); tip-deflection/length <= 0.10
(G2); mesh reproduction within 2.0% of the closed form (G3);
max_von_mises REPORTED-ONLY, never validated (G4 — the clamped-corner
singularity rises with refinement here too, measured 4.246e7 -> 4.670e7
Pa); and THE ELEMENT-ORDER BOUND (G5): only element_degree >= 2 is
validated. element_degree is typed input this instrument exposes and its
sibling does not: a degree-1 run is ACCEPTED by the wrapper, converges
cleanly, and reports a shear-locked, confidently wrong number (measured
0.28x the closed form at mesh_density 8, still 5.5% too stiff at 64,
with degree 2 at 0.987x on the coarsest mesh) and nothing in the
diagnostics says so. This bound must survive into every routing
decision, or routing to this substrate is unsafe. Note the tension
without glossing it: G1 demands slender beams because that is where the
reference is trustworthy, and slender beams are exactly where a locked
low-order element is MOST wrong — both are true at once, and G5 is what
makes G1's regime safely usable. An experiment spec's required "regime"
object for this substrate is {"notes": "..."}; a regime block carrying
Reynolds fields, an analysis_type key, or an operation key is rejected
by name by the per-substrate validator before anything runs.

4. HONEST LIMITS
  - Linear-elastic isotropic small-deflection statics ONLY. There is no
    plasticity, no hyperelasticity, no contact, no buckling, no dynamics, no
    anisotropy, no thermal coupling. A case whose physics is actually any of
    those will still return a number, and the wrapper cannot detect that.
  - ELEMENT DEGREE IS A REGIME BOUNDARY, NOT A PREFERENCE. A fully-integrated
    degree-1 Lagrange hex SHEAR-LOCKS in bending: it reports a beam that is far
    too stiff. Measured on this substrate, on the reference beam: degree 1
    returns 0.28x the closed-form tip deflection at mesh_density 8, and is still
    5.5% too stiff at mesh_density 64, while degree 2 is within 1.31% at
    mesh_density 8. Degree 1 is ACCEPTED by the typed input and IS NOT an error
    the wrapper reports -- a degree-1 run converges cleanly and returns a
    confident, wrong number. Only degree >= 2 is validated.
  - Refinement does not rescue a locked element, and the reason matters: locking
    severity is governed by ELEMENT ASPECT RATIO, not element count. Measured:
    refining ONLY through the thickness (holding 8 elements along the length)
    moved degree 1 from 0.2800x to 0.2894x of the closed form -- essentially
    nothing, across an 8x increase in through-thickness elements. Refining along
    the length helps substantially but plateaus short of correct (0.86x at 128
    elements along the length). Degree 2 needs neither: it sits at 0.987x on the
    very coarsest 8x1x1 mesh.
  - Shear locking (degree-1 bending stiffness; fixed by degree >= 2) and
    VOLUMETRIC locking (near-incompressibility as nu approaches 0.5) are two
    DIFFERENT diseases. Degree 2 does NOT fix volumetric locking; the remedies
    for that are mixed/u-p formulations, selective reduced integration, or F-bar,
    none of which this instrument has. A case with nu near 0.5 is numerically
    suspect even though the input is well-formed and the solve converges.
  - The Euler-Bernoulli closed form delta = P*L^3/(3*E*I) with I = w*h^3/12 is the
    only reference this instrument is validated against, and it is only itself
    trustworthy for SLENDER beams -- it neglects shear deformation, whose
    correction grows rapidly below length/height = 10. Note the tension honestly:
    the regime where the reference is most valid (slender) is the regime where a
    naive low-order element is most wrong. Both are true at once.
  - max_von_mises is REPORTED, NOT VALIDATED. Its pointwise maximum sits at the
    clamped-corner stress singularity, which belongs to the continuum problem
    itself: it rises with refinement instead of settling (measured at degree 2:
    4.246e7 -> 4.492e7 -> 4.670e7 Pa across mesh_density 8 -> 16 -> 32) and has no
    converged value to find. At degree 1 it is additionally corrupted by its own
    extraction: the degree-0 sample points sit at cell centres, which on a
    one-element-thick mesh lie exactly on the beam's neutral axis where bending
    stress vanishes -- measured 6.93e5 Pa at 8x1x1 versus 5.80e6 Pa at 8x1x2, an
    8x swing from a mesh change that should barely matter.
  - There is NO regime check anywhere in this instrument. It confirms that the
    solve ran and the output parsed -- never that the physics is in-regime, never
    that the mesh is converged, never that the element is appropriate. Slenderness,
    linearity, and locking are all invisible to it.

5. CANONICAL PARAMETER VOCABULARY
The wrapper honors exactly these canonical parameter names; anything else is
rejected by name, and every one is REQUIRED (there are no defaults -- an omitted
field is a rejection, never a guess):
  - length          (m)   -- beam length, spanning X; clamped at x=0
  - width           (m)   -- section width, spanning Y
  - height          (m)   -- section height, spanning Z; the load direction
  - E               (Pa)  -- Young's modulus; must be positive
  - nu              (-)   -- Poisson's ratio; must be in (-1, 0.5)
  - tip_load        (N)   -- total transverse load at x=length, in -Z,
                             distributed uniformly over the tip face
  - mesh_density    (int) -- hexahedral element count along the length; the width
                             and height counts scale by aspect ratio, so the
                             reference beam meshes 8 -> 8x1x1, 16 -> 16x1x1,
                             32 -> 32x2x2
  - element_degree  (int) -- Lagrange polynomial degree; >= 1 accepted, >= 2
                             validated. See the honest limits: this field is the
                             difference between a trustworthy number and a
                             confident wrong one.
The first seven names carry the SAME units and semantics as the sibling CalculiX
cantilever family v1, deliberately, so one beam can be posed to both instruments;
element_degree is this family's own and has no CalculiX counterpart (that solver's
C3D8I incompatible-modes element fixes locking in the element formulation instead,
which is why it has no such knob).


ROUTABLE SUBSTRATE: sympy_symbolic_exact
SUBSTRATE CONTRACT: sympy_symbolic_exact

1. WHAT THE INSTRUMENT IS
This substrate performs exact symbolic computer algebra over a single
closed-form expression: SymPy running inside an ephemeral, no-network,
memory-capped container, driven through the run_scipy wrapper —
deterministic Python with no AI inside, which validates the typed request
field-by-field, runs one operation in a restricted parse namespace, and
independently verifies the answer before returning it. One operation per
job, on one expression typed as text, over symbols the caller declares
explicitly. It is exact where it succeeds — a returned antiderivative is a
real antiderivative, checked by differentiating it back — and honest where
it fails, because SymPy frequently returns an operation UNEVALUATED rather
than wrong; that third outcome is neither an answer nor an error and is
carried as its own state (section 3). The validated envelope comes from
this substrate's own calibration jobs: all seven operations exercised live,
worst verified residual 4.05e-10 across 33 verified jobs (a diff, the
binding arm — only 2.47x inside the ruled 1e-9 tolerance). Cases in that
class are proven; anything far outside it is unproven, not impossible.
Operations offered: integrate_definite, integrate_indefinite, diff, limit,
series, solve, dsolve. An operation outside that closed set (minimization,
numeric quadrature as the answer, multi-expression systems, and the rest of
mathematics) is out of this regime by ruling S1 — deferred to the right
instrument, never best-effort translated into a nearby operation.

2. WHAT A CASE MUST DEFINE
A case is a typed request, not a file. It must define:
  - operation: exactly one of the seven listed in section 1.
  - expression: the closed-form expression as text. It is parsed in a
    RESTRICTED namespace against an AST allowlist: elementary and special
    functions (sin/cos/tan and inverses, hyperbolics, exp, log, sqrt, Abs,
    gamma, erf, factorial, atan2), structural forms (Derivative, Integral,
    Function), and the constants pi, E, I, oo, zoo, nan. Anything else is
    rejected BY NAME before any container starts.
  - symbols: every free name in the expression, declared explicitly. SymPy
    silently auto-creates symbols for typos, so the wrapper checks this
    itself — an undeclared name is rejected, not guessed.
  - assumptions (optional): per-symbol declarations from the closed set
    {real, positive, negative, nonnegative, nonzero, integer, rational,
    complex, finite}. Declaring an assumption CHANGES THE MATHEMATICAL
    MEANING of the job (sqrt(x**2) is x under positive=True and Abs(x)
    under the complex default) — see section 4.
  - per-operation fields: integrate_definite needs var, lower, upper;
    integrate_indefinite needs var; diff needs var (optional order); limit
    needs var, point; series needs var, point (optional order); solve needs
    var; dsolve needs var, func (optional ics, e.g. {"y(0)": 3}). Bounds and
    points are themselves expressions and go through the same AST allowlist.
Unknown fields are rejected by name. One operation per job; a second
quantity means a second job.

3. WHAT run_scipy RETURNS TODAY
On a run that completes, a small fixed summary — never raw container output:
  - valid: true or false. False means NO result is reported, for any reason.
  - state: exactly one of three, NEVER collapsed into two:
      solved_verified — SymPy found a closed form AND the wrapper
        independently verified it (back-substitution; a root substituted
        back; checkodesol for ODEs; numeric spot-checks for diff/series).
        The ONLY state that carries a result out of the wrapper.
      unevaluated — SymPy DECLINED: the operation survives unperformed in
        the output (the canonical instance is the indefinite integral of
        x**x, which has no elementary closed form), or the operation call
        raised its narrow decline set (NotImplementedError or PoleError,
        rulings S4a/S4b — by exception TYPE, never message text). An HONEST
        NON-ANSWER: result null, reason null, the substrate worked
        correctly. It must never be narrated as an error and never leak as
        a QoI.
      error — invalid input, a container kill (memory cap or timeout), or
        verification_failed: SymPy returned a closed form the wrapper could
        not confirm. A solved-but-unverified answer is an error — NO RESULT
        LEAVES THIS WRAPPER UNVERIFIED (residual tolerance 1e-9, ruled S2;
        the residual verifies the RETURNED object, ruled S2a).
  - result: the exact expression or scalar AS A STRING, non-null only in
    solved_verified. Exact means exact: "pi/2", not 1.5707963.
  - residual: the verification residual (worse of back-substitution and the
    returned-object check). crosscheck: for definite integrals and ODEs
    with a declared initial condition, an independent-algorithm arm (quad /
    solve_ivp) — DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, agreement is evidence, never proof, and
    disagreement is a flag for a human, never auto-resolved.
  - reason: a named, machine-greppable failure reason, non-null only in
    error. diagnostics: a bounded honest line (<= 800 characters).
  - runtime_s: wall-clock seconds.
Indicative cost, measured on this substrate: 0.6-1.8 s of wall clock per
job, container-startup-dominated rather than compute-dominated — an
unevaluated non-answer costs the same as a solved answer, so cost predicts
nothing about success. Runs are killed after 600 seconds and reported as a
named failure; nothing in this regime has approached that.
How this summary maps to an upstream stage-4 run entry (Packet B Phase 1.0
ruling, items 3/4, owner 2026-07-17): converged := (valid is true). For
this substrate, converged means the job COMPLETED AND THE WRAPPER ANSWERED
— true for solved_verified AND for unevaluated (the honest non-answer is a
completed answer about the question), false only for error. The wrapper's
state travels verbatim in the entry's optional `state` key, and the answer
slot is per-state: solved_verified carries qoi_expression — the exact
result STRING, never a fabricated float; unevaluated carries the wrapper's
own honest-non-answer diagnostics line as qoi_error, with state
"unevaluated" beside it saying machine-readably that this is a decline, not
a failure; error carries the diagnostics line as qoi_error with state
"error". No number is ever invented at this mapping.
THIS INSTRUMENT'S REGIME (regime stated at enrollment per R-23.5-5c; shape
ruled Packet B Phase 1.0, owner, 2026-07-17): not a Reynolds band and not a
circuit analysis — the regime of an exact symbolic instrument is which
operation it performs on the expression as typed. An experiment spec's
required "regime" object for this substrate is
  {"operation": "integrate_definite" | "integrate_indefinite" | "diff" |
   "limit" | "series" | "solve" | "dsolve", "notes": "..."}
where the seven operations are the wrapper's own closed operation allowlist
(ruling S1, section 2) — the same closed set whose boundary section 1
declares out of regime by ruling: a question outside it is deferred to the
right instrument, never best-effort translated into a nearby operation. A
regime block carrying Reynolds fields, an analysis_type key, an operation
outside that set, or a missing operation is rejected by the per-substrate
validator before anything runs.

4. HONEST LIMITS
  - THE CENTRAL LIMIT: the result is trustworthy as a statement about THE
    EXPRESSION AS TYPED, and about nothing else. Whether that expression
    models the question the caller meant is a SEPARATE claim this substrate
    cannot adjudicate: an exactly correct integral of sin(x) over [0, pi]
    is a worthless answer to a question about the MEAN value of sin(x), and
    sin(30) is exactly correct in radians while being the wrong model of a
    claim about degrees. Both return solved_verified with a true result.
    This substrate's failure mode is not a wrong number — it is an exactly
    right answer to the wrong question, indistinguishable at the gate from
    a genuine success (ruling S3: trust the narrow symbolic claim AND defer
    the modeling/utility claim in the same breath, never a bare trust).
  - Assumptions and branch cuts are a KNOWN GAP, not a check (S5): the
    wrapper validates that declared assumptions are allowlist members, but
    whether the declared set matches the caller's INTENT lives nowhere the
    wrapper or the gate can read. SymPy's defaults are COMPLEX. Advisory
    only; its silence is not evidence of agreement.
  - An unevaluated result is an answer about the question, not a failure to
    be retried. Re-asking will not create a closed form that does not
    exist; the honest route is to the right instrument (S4).
  - Verification independence is tiered, and no arm is independent of
    SymPy's own translation layer: back-substitution/checkodesol/limit are
    SymPy checking SymPy; diff/series spot-checks run on numpy through
    lambdify (partial); definite integrals and ics-bearing ODEs get a
    genuinely different algorithm (quad / solve_ivp) that still reaches
    numpy through lambdify. Every arm was fault-injected and rejects a
    deliberately wrong result, with the characterized exceptions below.
  - The limit arm FAILS CLOSED on slowly-converging limits: its residual is
    the function's genuine remaining distance from its limit at a finite
    probe, so sin(x)/x verifies while (exp(x)-1)/x is REJECTED as
    verification_failed despite SymPy being exactly right. A limit reported
    as verification_failed may mean the arm is too weak to confirm it, not
    that the answer is wrong.
  - The series truncation check is BLIND to a wrong coefficient on the
    HIGHEST RETAINED term (structural, not a tuning oversight); low- and
    mid-order errors are caught.
  - A DIVERGENT definite integral returns solved_verified with result 'oo'
    or even 'nan' at residual 0.0 (measured: sec(x)**2 over [0, pi];
    1/x over [-1, 1]) — SymPy is not wrong, those integrals diverge, but a
    NON-FINITE result must NEVER be read as a QoI. Whether such a case
    should instead be unevaluated is an open owner question, NOT ruled.
  - Whether a case's regime assumptions are themselves trustworthy is NOT
    checked anywhere in this contract; that open axis belongs to the
    fidelity gate's future work, and nothing here should be read as
    covering it.

5. CANONICAL PARAMETER VOCABULARY
Unlike the cavity substrate, this instrument takes no named physical-
parameter dictionary: the expression itself is the parameterization. The
wrapper honors exactly these typed keys:
  - operation    (enum)          — see section 1
  - expression   (string)        — AST-allowlisted expression text
  - symbols      (list of names) — every free name in the expression
  - assumptions  (object, opt.)  — per-symbol, from the closed set in
                                   section 2
  - var          (name)          — the operating variable (all operations)
  - lower, upper (expressions)   — integrate_definite bounds
  - point        (expression)    — limit / series expansion point
  - order        (integer >= 1)  — diff / series order, optional
  - func         (name)          — dsolve's unknown function
  - ics          (object, opt.)  — dsolve initial conditions, keys are
                                   expressions (e.g. "y(0)"), values numbers
Every field is validated by name pre-solve; a missing, unknown, or
ill-typed field is rejected before anything runs. Bounds, points, and ics
keys are expressions and pass the same AST allowlist as the expression
itself.


ROUTABLE SUBSTRATE: ngspice_linear_passive
SUBSTRATE CONTRACT: ngspice_linear_passive

1. WHAT THE INSTRUMENT IS
This substrate solves ideal lumped linear passive networks: circuits built from
resistors, inductors, capacitors, ideal independent voltage/current sources, and
linear controlled sources. The solver is ngspice 42 running inside a container,
driven through the run_ngspice wrapper — deterministic Python with no AI inside,
which composes the whole deck (the caller supplies element lines only), runs it,
and reads the resulting log. The validated envelope comes from this substrate's
own self-checks: a resistive divider, a single-pole RC low-pass (tau = 1 ms,
corner ~1 kHz), and a series RLC at damping ratio zeta = 0.2, each agreeing with
closed-form circuit theory. Cases near that class are proven; anything far
outside it is unproven, not impossible.
Analyses offered: .op, .dc, .ac, .tran. An analysis outside that set (noise, pz,
disto, and the rest of ngspice's reach) is out of this regime by ruling.

2. WHAT A CASE MUST DEFINE
A case is a typed request, not a file. It must define:
  - netlist_body: the circuit's element lines ONLY. No dot-commands and no
    .control block — the wrapper owns all of those, including the analysis
    statement itself. A netlist line beginning with '.' is rejected.
  - analysis: exactly one of
      {"type": "op"}
      {"type": "dc",   "source", "start", "stop", "step"}
      {"type": "ac",   "variation": "dec"|"lin"|"oct", "n", "fstart", "fstop"}
      {"type": "tran", "tstep", "tstop", "tmax"}
  - qoi: {"kind": "node_voltage" | "vsource_current", "target": <node or source
    name>, "reduction": <see section 3>, "at": <float or null>}
Allowed element letters, first character of the line, case-insensitive:
    R  resistor                     L  inductor
    C  capacitor                    V  independent voltage source
    I  independent current source   E  linear voltage-controlled voltage source
    F  linear current-controlled current source
    G  linear voltage-controlled current source
    H  linear current-controlled voltage source
Banned element letters, each rejected by letter and line number pre-solve:
    D Q M J B T O U S W A X K N P, and any unknown letter.
K (coupled inductors) is excluded from v1 DELIBERATELY: mutual coupling is
linear and would fit this regime, but it is untested here. That is an OPEN CARD
QUESTION, not an oversight.
An R/L/C line must be EXACTLY '<name> <node+> <node-> <value>' — four tokens,
with a value that parses as a SPICE number and is strictly positive. On E/F/G/H
lines the POLY, TABLE and value= forms are rejected. A '{' anywhere in the body
is rejected. Component values accept the SPICE suffixes f p n u m mil k meg g t,
where m is MILLI and meg is 1e6.

3. WHAT run_ngspice RETURNS TODAY
On a run that completes, a small fixed summary — never the full solver log:
  - valid: true or false. False means NO number is reported, for any reason.
  - qoi: ONE scalar per run, or null. The reduction is applied in Python, never
    in ngspice measurement scripting:
      op_value    — the single operating-point value (.op only)
      final       — the value at the last solved point
      max | min   — the extremum over all solved points
      value_at    — the value interpolated at "at" (time for .tran, frequency
                    for .ac, sweep value for .dc); linear in the sweep variable,
                    log-frequency for .ac
      corner_3db  — the -3 dB corner frequency (.ac only), by log-frequency
                    interpolation at |H| = |H_dc|/sqrt(2); the returned
                    diagnostics carry the run's own estimated fstart bias
  - diagnostics: a bounded, honest, human-readable line (<= 800 characters).
    Never the raw deck or log.
  - runtime_s: wall-clock seconds.
A QoI is NEVER returned when any failure marker appears in the log, when the
output file is missing or empty, when the requested vector does not exist, or
when the extracted value is not finite. The instrument does not fabricate a
number: the exit code alone is not trusted, because a broken circuit can exit 0
(see section 4).
Indicative cost, measured on this substrate: 0.19-0.85 s of wall clock per solve
(median 0.26 s, n=31), dominated by container-exec overhead rather than by the
solve — the circuits themselves solve in milliseconds, and a 30,023-row
transient differs from a 3-element steady solve by well under 3x. Runs are
killed after 600 seconds and reported as a failure; nothing in this regime has
approached that.
How this summary maps to an upstream stage-4 run entry (ruled R1 option 4,
2026-07-17): converged := (valid is true). For this substrate, converged means
the run COMPLETED AND PARSED — the deck ran, no failure marker fired, and one
finite scalar was extracted. It does NOT mean an iterative-residual criterion
was met: this instrument has none — a linear network solve either completes or
it does not, and agreement with circuit theory is judged separately (section 4).
valid=false maps to converged=false with the diagnostics line carried as
qoi_error, and no number. This substrate carries no optional `state` value: the
summary has no state vocabulary of its own beyond the boolean valid.
THIS INSTRUMENT'S REGIME (ruled R-23.5-5, 2026-07-17): not a Reynolds band —
the regime of a linear passive network is which analysis it lives in. An
experiment spec's required "regime" object for this substrate is
  {"analysis_type": "op" | "dc" | "ac" | "tran", "notes": "..."}
where the four analysis types are the wrapper's own typed analysis set
(section 2) — the same set whose boundary section 1 declares out of regime by
ruling. A regime block carrying Reynolds fields, an analysis_type outside
that set, or a missing analysis_type is rejected by the per-substrate
validator before anything runs.

4. HONEST LIMITS
  - Ideal linear passive only. There are no semiconductor device models, no
    behavioral sources, no transmission lines, no subcircuits, and no
    nonlinearity of any kind. A hypothesis whose physics needs them is outside
    this instrument, and the regime screen rejects the netlist rather than
    silently approximating it.
  - QoI values characterize the ideal netlist exactly as provided; no physical-
    board effects (trace parasitics, component tolerance, ESR, non-ideal ground)
    are represented. A result here is a statement about a schematic, not about a
    manufactured board.
  - The solver's exit code is NOT a sufficient failure signal, and two measured
    failures prove it. (i) A floating node (no DC path to ground) fails the
    operating-point solve, falls through gmin and source stepping, then succeeds
    at a transient operating point, prints a plausible voltage, and EXITS 0. The
    wrapper catches this by scanning the log for failure markers. (ii) A
    zero-valued resistor emits NO marker at all, exits 0, and reports a
    fabricated 1000 A through the short; only the pre-solve value screen catches
    it. A third, found by screening ngspice's own shipped test suite: a trailing
    per-analysis override (`R1 in out 1k ac=100k`) runs clean and silently
    simulates a value other than the one written, which is why R/L/C arity is
    fixed at four tokens.
  - ONE scalar QoI per run. There is no vector of QoIs, no time series, no field
    export, and no second quantity from the same solve — a second quantity means
    a second run.
  - An extremum QoI (max/min) is a discretization-artifact suspect and must be
    screened before it is trusted: the value is only meaningful if it is stable
    as the timestep tightens. MEASURED example on this substrate, series RLC at
    zeta = 0.2 (analytic peak 1.5266236763): max(v_out) overshoots the analytic
    peak by 4.84e-03 ABSOLUTE (3.17e-03 relative) at tmax = 10 us, 5.57e-05
    (3.65e-05 rel) at 1 us, and 4.74e-07 (3.10e-07 rel) at 0.1 us — a monotone
    settle onto the closed-form answer, so this particular extremum IS
    trustworthy at tmax <= 1 us. An extremum whose gap does NOT shrink this way
    is tracking the grid, not the physics. Note the units: the settle figures
    above are absolute gaps; the reproduction tolerance is relative.
  - For .tran, tmax is the refinement lever, not tstep — and it is a ONE-WAY
    lever. MEASURED: tmax is a CEILING on the solver's step, not a target, so a
    tmax coarser than ngspice's own adaptive error control is simply inert
    (every tmax from 4e-5 to 2e-4 on the zeta=0.2 RLC returns the identical peak
    1.52415539 from an identical 144 data rows). A .tran run cannot be coarsened
    past its adaptive floor — only refined. MEASURED further: tstep does not
    control the written grid at all; wrdata emits one row per INTERNAL timestep
    (row count ~ tstop/tmax), unchanged across a 50x tstep range, so an extremum
    is always sampled on the solver's grid and never on the print grid.
    Consequently the band where tmax binds but is still too coarse is narrow,
    and inside it the peak error is NON-MONOTONE and flips sign — the monotone-
    settle screen is only meaningful on a ladder wholly inside the fine region.
    MEASURED, RC step at tau = 1 ms: the relative error at t = tau falls
    4.97e-05 -> 6.71e-07 -> 2.80e-07 as tmax tightens 50 us -> 5 us -> 0.5 us,
    and the worst error over [0, 5*tau] falls 2.60e-03 -> 2.88e-05 -> 4.79e-06.
  - A corner_3db QoI carries a systematic bias set by fstart, NOT by the
    frequency grid. |H_dc| is proxied by the magnitude at the lowest solved
    frequency, which biases a one-pole corner HIGH by a relative
    (fstart/fcorner)^2. MEASURED: +9.94e-05 at fstart = 10 Hz, +9.96e-07 at
    1 Hz, +7.51e-09 at 0.1 Hz, against a predicted 1e-04 / 1e-06 / 1e-08.
    Refining the grid from 10 to 100 points per decade moved the same corner by
    only 3.79e-06 relative — roughly 26x LESS than the fstart bias it sat inside.
    Reading the grid-density delta as the corner's error bar understates it by
    that factor; start the sweep at least three decades below the expected
    corner. Each corner_3db run reports its own estimated bias in diagnostics.
  - Convergence is not this instrument's risk; agreement with closed-form theory
    is. A linear network has an exact answer, so a result that disagrees with
    circuit theory means the request was mis-posed or under-resolved, not that
    the physics is subtle.
  - Whether a case's regime assumptions are themselves trustworthy is NOT
    checked anywhere in this contract; that open axis belongs to the fidelity
    gate's future work, and nothing here should be read as covering it.

5. CANONICAL PARAMETER VOCABULARY
Unlike the cavity substrate, this instrument takes no named physical-parameter
dictionary: the circuit itself is the parameterization, written as element lines
in netlist_body. The wrapper honors exactly these typed keys:
  - netlist_body   (string)  — circuit element lines only, <= 200 lines / 20 kB
  - analysis.type  (enum)    — op | dc | ac | tran
  - analysis.*     (numbers) — the fields listed in section 2 for that type
  - qoi.kind       (enum)    — node_voltage | vsource_current
  - qoi.target     (name)    — a node name, or a voltage-source name for current
  - qoi.reduction  (enum)    — op_value | final | max | min | value_at | corner_3db
  - qoi.at         (number)  — required for value_at, forbidden otherwise
Every field is validated by name pre-solve; a missing, unknown, or ill-typed
field is rejected before anything runs. Component values live inside
netlist_body in SPICE notation, not as separate parameters.


ROUTABLE SUBSTRATE: rdkit
SUBSTRATE CONTRACT — rdkit, descriptor_computation

1. WHAT THIS IS.
A deterministic cheminformatics calculator (RDKit) that computes 2D molecular
descriptors from a single small molecule supplied as a SMILES string. It is an
ANSWER-class instrument: the descriptor it returns IS its exact computed output
for the parsed molecule, not a prediction or an estimate. It runs no model, no
simulation, and no experiment.

2. TYPED INPUT.
    smiles   : the molecule, a SMILES string RDKit can parse AND sanitize.
    quantity : which descriptor to return, one of the fixed allowlist below.
The molecule as written is the parameterization; there is no separate parameter
dictionary. A SMILES that does not parse-and-sanitize under RDKit's own valence
model yields no number.

3. REGIME (the (substrate, regime) card unit — descriptor_computation).
In-regime: a valid, sanitizable, single small organic molecule, and a
descriptor on the fixed allowlist (2D graph/constitution descriptors only:
MolWt, ExactMolWt, HeavyAtomCount, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors,
NumRotatableBonds, TPSA, MolLogP, NumAromaticRings, RingCount, FractionCSP3,
NOCount). Out of regime, by construction: any ML-PREDICTED property (solubility,
ADMET, activity), any 3D/conformer-dependent quantity, reactions, or a
descriptor outside the allowlist. These are rejected or unrepresentable, not
approximated.

4. WHAT IT RETURNS.
One scalar QoI — the requested allowlist descriptor for the molecule — plus a
bounded diagnostic string. It never returns a raw structure, a descriptor for an
unparseable molecule, or a non-finite value.

5. QoI EXTRACTION AND THE ONE KNOWN GAP.
The QoI is the named descriptor, computed deterministically (identical SMILES ->
identical value). THE KNOWN GAP (uncheckable by the gate): a computed descriptor
is a PROXY for a molecular property, never a measured one. In particular MolLogP
is Crippen's COMPUTED logP, not an experimental logP; TPSA is a topological
estimate of polar surface area, not a measured one. Trust the number as RDKit's
exact computation of that descriptor; do NOT read it as an experimental
measurement of the underlying physical property.


ROUTABLE SUBSTRATE: cobrapy
SUBSTRATE CONTRACT — cobrapy, fba_steady_state

1. WHAT THIS IS.
A constraint-based flux-balance analysis (FBA) calculator (COBRApy + an LP
solver) that computes the maximum steady-state biomass flux ("growth rate") of a
genome-scale metabolic model. It is a FILTER-class instrument: the growth it
reports is a feasible steady-state optimum — a RELATIVE screen for comparing
models/conditions — NOT a measured in-vivo growth rate. It is a deterministic
linear program: no kinetics, no regulation, no dynamics.

2. TYPED INPUT.
    model      : one of the baked allowlist models (a small textbook model and a
                 genome-scale model of the same organism).
    quantity   : the QoI to return (the fixed-summary vocabulary; the growth
                 rate).
    min_growth : OPTIONAL. A biomass lower-bound feasibility constraint; a value
                 the network cannot support makes the solve INFEASIBLE.

3. REGIME (the (substrate, regime) card unit — fba_steady_state).
In-regime: a baked allowlist model, solved at steady state for its maximum
biomass flux. Out of regime, by construction: kinetics/dynamics (dFBA),
regulation, transient behaviour, any model outside the allowlist, and any claim
about an absolute measured growth rate.

4. WHAT IT RETURNS.
One scalar QoI — the optimal growth rate — gated on the SOLVER STATUS. It never
returns a growth number for a non-optimal (infeasible / unbounded / errored)
solve; on any non-optimal status the QoI is absent.

5. THE STATUS GATE AND THE KNOWN GAP.
The QoI is trustworthy ONLY when the LP status is `optimal`. An FBA solver
exposes a stale objective value even after an infeasible solve; this substrate
NEVER surfaces it — non-optimal status yields no number. THE KNOWN GAP
(uncheckable by the gate): the FBA optimum is a feasible steady-state upper bound
under the model's stoichiometry and media, NOT a measured growth rate. Trust it
as a relative feasibility/growth screen; do NOT read it as an experimental
measurement, and do not assume the model/media/objective suit the question.


ROUTABLE SUBSTRATE: homology_search
SUBSTRATE CONTRACT — homology_search

1. WHAT THIS IS.
A local sequence-homology search (BLAST; HMMER as a second backend) that scores
how significantly a query sequence resembles entries in a reference database,
via Karlin-Altschul e-value statistics. It is a FILTER-class instrument: the
e-value is the SIGNIFICANCE of similarity — a relative screen, not homology or
function.

2. TYPED INPUT.
    database  : a baked allowlist reference database.
    query     : a protein sequence.
    tool      : the backend, one of {blast, hmmer} (an explicit choice).
    quantity  : the QoI (the best-hit e-value).

3. REGIME (homology_search).
In-regime: a protein query, a baked database, a similarity search returning an
e-value. Out of regime: databases outside the allowlist, non-sequence inputs, and
any homology/orthology/function claim beyond similarity significance.

4. WHAT IT RETURNS.
One scalar QoI — the best (minimum) e-value — returned ONLY when the search
provably ran (a valid database, no search error). A clean run that finds nothing
is a real 'no significant homolog' result (no e-value), DISTINCT from a search
that could not run.

5. THE DID-IT-WORK GATE AND THE KNOWN GAP.
BLAST exits 0 even when the database is missing/malformed — so exit code is not
trusted; a search error on stderr means the search could NOT run (defer), never
a '0 hits'. THE KNOWN GAP (uncheckable): a significant e-value is the significance
of SIMILARITY, not homology, orthology, or function; low-complexity and
composition bias also inflate significance. Trust the e-value as a
similarity-significance screen, not as a homology/function determination.


ROUTABLE SUBSTRATE: mafft
SUBSTRATE CONTRACT — mafft, msa_alignment

1. WHAT THIS IS.
A multiple sequence alignment tool (MAFFT): it arranges two or more sequences
into columns of putative homology. It carries the NARROWEST trust claim of the
instruments here — an alignment it produces is a heuristic hypothesis about how
sequences relate, not a determination that the alignment is correct.

2. TYPED INPUT.
    sequences : a list of >= 2 sequences, all over the SAME alphabet (all
                protein OR all nucleotide), each non-empty and valid.
    quantity  : the QoI (the alignment-identity statistic).

3. REGIME (msa_alignment).
In-regime: >= 2 alignable same-alphabet sequences, aligned, summarized by a
descriptive identity statistic. Out of regime: alignment CORRECTNESS or
phylogenetic inference; mixed-alphabet or single-sequence input; scores beyond
average pairwise identity.

4. WHAT IT RETURNS.
One scalar QoI — the average pairwise percent identity over the computed
alignment (DESCRIPTIVE). It returns nothing for un-alignable input (refused
before running) or a malformed alignment.

5. THE INPUT GATE AND THE KNOWN GAP.
Alignment is near-total: garbage in yields a well-formed alignment OF the
garbage. So "an alignment was produced" is NOT evidence it means anything; the
trustworthiness gate is on the INPUT (>= 2 valid same-alphabet sequences),
checked before running. THE KNOWN GAP (uncheckable, and it is the whole
scientific question): a well-formed alignment is a HEURISTIC homology hypothesis,
guide-tree-dependent — a different tool or setting gives a different alignment.
Trust the alignment DESCRIPTIVELY, never as the biologically correct one.


MACHINE CAPABILITY TABLE — the ONLY parameter names each instrument can accept, and the ONLY quantities it can return. This is the exact set the router checks against; a hypothesis needing anything not listed here CANNOT BE RUN, no matter how good the science is.
  cavity_2d_cfd
      can vary   : cavity_length, end_time, kinematic_viscosity, lid_velocity, mesh_resolution, reynolds_number, time_step
      can measure: (see contract)
  calculix_cantilever_fea
      can vary   : E, height, length, mesh_density, nu, tip_load, width
      can measure: tip_displacement, max_von_mises
  fenicsx_cantilever_elastic
      can vary   : E, element_degree, height, length, mesh_density, nu, tip_load, width
      can measure: tip_displacement, max_von_mises
  sympy_symbolic_exact
      can vary   : assumptions, expression, func, ics, lower, operation, order, point, symbols, upper, var
      can measure: (see contract)
  ngspice_linear_passive
      can vary   : analysis, netlist_body, qoi
      can measure: (see contract)
  rdkit
      can vary   : quantity, smiles
      can measure: MolWt, ExactMolWt, HeavyAtomCount, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, TPSA, MolLogP, NumAromaticRings, RingCount, FractionCSP3, NOCount
  cobrapy
      can vary   : min_growth, model, quantity
      can measure: growth_rate
      model MUST be one of: e_coli_core, iML1515
  homology_search
      can vary   : database, quantity, query, tool
      can measure: e_value
      database MUST be one of: demo_prot, _broken_selftest
      tool MUST be one of: blast, hmmer
  mafft
      can vary   : quantity, sequences
      can measure: alignment_identity

HARD CONSTRAINT, not a preference. Every hypothesis you propose must be testable AS-IS by at least one instrument above — meaning the experiment that would test it varies ONLY parameter names listed in that instrument's 'can vary' line, and its quantity of interest is one of that instrument's 'can measure' entries. Before you write a hypothesis, name the instrument that would test it and check both lines. A hypothesis requiring a knob or a measurement not listed there cannot be run at all and is worth nothing here, however novel or well-motivated — propose a different one that fits an instrument as it actually is. Do not assume a parameter exists because it would be physically sensible, and do not rename a parameter to make it look like one that is listed.
